claims.text: A thin molybdenum interlayer can effectively mediate bonding between tungsten and CuCrZr.
The molybdenum interlayer can accommodate thermal-expansion differences between tungsten and CuCrZr.
The molybdenum interlayer can mitigate chemical incompatibilities between tungsten and CuCrZr.
The proposed molybdenum film is 1–3 μm thick and deposited by physical vapor deposition.
The proposed post-deposition treatment is annealing at 900°C for 1 hour in vacuum.
Molybdenum has a coefficient of thermal expansion intermediate between those of tungsten and CuCrZr.
Molybdenum is chemically compatible with both tungsten and CuCrZr.
The intermediate thermal expansion and chemical compatibility of molybdenum reduce interfacial thermal stress.
Reduced interfacial thermal stress prevents delamination and cracking under extreme conditions.
A molybdenum interlayer will increase W/CuCrZr bonding strength relative to direct bonding.
A molybdenum interlayer will reduce delamination relative to direct W-to-CuCrZr bonding.
A molybdenum interlayer will maintain interfacial structural integrity during thermal cycling and irradiation.
Direct W-to-CuCrZr bonding is prone to failure because of thermal-expansion mismatch and chemical incompatibility.
The efficacy of the molybdenum interlayer may change when thermal-cycle or irradiation conditions deviate from those of fusion-reactor operation.
The long-term behavior of the molybdenum interlayer under continuous irradiation and extreme thermal cycling is uncertain.
